title: Hippo indexer master: which store answers what and how to reach it
desc: Expert map of the wkhippo indexers: the SQLite keyword cache with scan range, the studied json index, the chatlog shards, which commands really use them, measured timings, traps, and the direction to converge on one indexer
steps: STORES AND WHO USES THEM (measured 2026-09-26). One: SQLite keyword cache C:/Users/***/.wkharness/hippo-index.db, tables keyword_cache (keyword, session_id, family, time, matches, preview, updated_at) and keyword_scan_range (keyword, oldest_unix, newest_unix), driven by D:/GitHub/personal-docs/tools/global_indexer.py with four subcommands query, get_scan_range, update, update_scan_range. Consumers are Invoke-WkHippoRecent.ps1 (query line 167, range lines 194 to 236) and Invoke-WkHippoStudied.ps1 (range writes). Canonical wkhippo.ps1 recall has NO reference to it, a recall probe took about 44 s cold and 40 s warm and left the db untouched. Two: studied json index C:/Users/***/.wkharness/wkhippo-studied-index.json (schema v3, records plus inverted skill index plus offsets) used by Get-WkStudiedFromIndex and Get-WkAsyncPendingFromIndex. Three: chatlog index and shards under the user profile .wkhippo folder, about 1.7 GB, an 82 percent mirror of its sources, measured slower than grep.

HOW TO ASK A SESSION QUESTION. Last calls and file path: wkhippo trace SID --last N (first line prints family and file path, works for claude and codex, the wkroot sid maps to a transcript). Prior art: wkhippo recall KEYWORDS (default 7 days and this repo only, --days N, --since ISO, --alltime, --all) and wkhippo foresee APPROACH. Pending agents and skills read: the studied index functions. Regex over many sessions with a cache: the target interface is wkhippo index REGEX (days or since or alltime, sessions, family, json) which is being built, check wkappbot skill read global-indexer-usage for its status before building anything.

DIRECTION (owner 2026-09-26). One indexer: the SQLite cache with scan ranges, reached by one wkhippo index command. The db is regenerated weekly, a week starts Monday 00:00 GMT, one file per week named with that Monday date. Past-week dbs are read-only reference and any missing range is scanned and stored into the current-week db only. Chatlog shards and the studied json are to be rebuilt on top of it after an equivalence check. agy history is SQLite and is opened read-only. Detail specs: global-indexer-usage steps 5 and 7, wkhippo-chatlog-unified-index steps 19 to 22, spokesman-hippo-advanced. //why:Studied hippo-indexer-master for session_index update //why:Studied hippo-indexer-master

TRAPS THAT COST ROUNDS. An empty-string argument is dropped by PowerShell so later arguments shift left, update derives the stored time from the file mtime, range 0,0 means no range was ever recorded and not an empty index, family name case differs between callers, a python spawn per lookup (about 96 ms) loses to a 50 ms direct read of one transcript so use the index for cross-session and cross-family questions only, and a zero-match query does not widen the recorded range. A helper found only in wkhippo.tmp is a proto copy and not the canonical tool, grep the canonical file before believing a sector that cites it. Two sectors read different files and reported opposite answers about recall, so always run the real command twice and read the db before and after.

SPEC INDEX-DRIVEN DISCOVERY (owner 2026-09-28): the index itself carries everything file discovery needs, so no wkhippo command walks the file system for files it already knows. (1) FOLDER rows: folder path and last seen folder mtime; a refresh enters a folder ONLY when its current mtime is newer than the recorded one (a gap exists) -- NTFS bumps a folder mtime when a file is created, deleted or renamed, so a new session always bumps it, and appends to known files are handled by (2). (2) SESSION rows: path, session id, family, cwd, session START time taken from the first 3 lines (read once; the first lines never change however big the session grows), size, mtime, LAST SEARCHED time and the byte OFFSET searched so far. (3) SID lookup reads only session rows (regex over the stored first-line fields); a miss enters only folders with a gap. (4) A keyword search reads only the bytes appended after the recorded offset of each candidate session and reuses cached matches for the part already searched; a session whose start and mtime are both outside the search window is never opened. (5) recent, trace, foresee and recall all pick candidate files from these rows. Verify: parity of results with the legacy path on real keywords, files touched and wall time before and after, and a second identical query that opens 0 files. Code home: wkappbot-kih tools/session_index.py and tools/global_indexer.py; consumers under WKAppBot bin. (10) RECORD FIELDS (owner 2026-09-28): each segment record per (keyword, session) carries three byte offsets, each paired with the time of its line: FIRST MATCH offset (segment start), LAST MATCH offset, and SCAN END offset (searched through here; the span after the last match up to scan end is a confirmed no-match). A gap search starts at the last record scan end; no new match only advances scan end; a new match sets the old record scan end to the line before it and opens a new record whose first match is that line; an all-lines segment has last match equal to scan end and stores no line payload. Matched lines (point 7) hang off the record. (9) SEGMENT RECORDS (owner 2026-09-28): when a gap search finds a NEW match, do not stretch the old record over it -- extend the old record only up to the line just before the first new match, and open a NEW record starting at that match; a stretch with no new match simply extends the last record in place. So each record is one homogeneous segment (a no-match span or a match span), existing records are never rewritten, and the record count grows only with match clusters, not with searches. (8) ALL-LINES MATCH IS STORED AS NULL (owner 2026-09-28): when a regex matches EVERY line of a searched range, store NO line payload at all, only the range itself (start and end byte offsets with the times of their first and last lines) -- an all-lines range means every line matched, read it directly from the file between those offsets, and the cached time-to-offset pairs also let any later time-window query seek straight to the right byte instead of scanning -- so a too-broad regex never duplicates a transcript into the DB. (7) MATCHED LINES ARE STORED RAW (owner 2026-09-28): for every match, store the matching JSONL line VERBATIM (the original JSON text, no transformation, no preview cut) plus its byte offset in the session file, so a repeated search is answered from the DB without opening any transcript; keep the offset so an oversized line can later be replaced by a seek if the DB grows too large. (6) ZERO MATCHES ARE RESULTS TOO (owner 2026-09-28): per (keyword, session) store the last searched time and byte offset EVEN WHEN NOTHING MATCHED -- searched up to X, none found is cached knowledge, so the next search reads only past X. This replaces the trap in step 4 (a zero-match query does not widen the recorded range), which today makes empty regions get rescanned on every call.

FIXED REGEX, FILTER AFTER (owner 2026-10-02): the cache key is the regex, so every distinct regex is a cold scan and a new cache row. WHEN: any sector, root or tool searches sessions through the indexer or wkgrdb. HOW: search with a small set of FIXED broad regexes (a stable keyword per topic such as a skill id, a root sid, an order file name) and narrow the result by FILTERING the returned rows in the caller (time window, family, repo, text contains), never by building a new regex per question. Reuse the exact same regex string byte for byte, so the second call opens zero files. WHY: a per-question regex never hits the cache and re-reads transcripts every time; a fixed regex plus a filter turns the cache into the answer. Verify with the second identical query printing scanned_files 0.
